body:
## Why

The durable tier lives at `refs/heads/kb-board`, so it shows up in `git branch`, in every branch picker,
and in GitHub's branch list — a branch nobody ever checks out, sitting among the ones that mean something.
The operator's objection (2026-09-03) is to that visibility, not to the mechanism.

Nothing about the design needs `refs/heads/`. Everything the tier relies on — plumbing writes,
`update-ref` as compare-and-swap, history, push and fetch — works on any ref namespace. hkb **already**
does this for claims, at `refs/kb/locks/<n>/<k>`.

Considered and rejected: moving the board to a user folder (`~/.hkb/…`, the way Hermes keeps
`~/.hermes/kanban.db`, "deliberately single-host", no sync). It has zero repo footprint, but it gives up
backup-without-user-action, needs a path-keying scheme that breaks when a directory moves or when one repo
has several worktrees — which hkb creates constantly — and loses `git log` as a history a human can read
with tools they already have. A hidden ref keeps all three and still answers the complaint.

**Measured before filing** (2026-09-03, against this repo's real remote), because the whole option depends
on it:

- `git push origin refs/kb/boards/probe:refs/kb/boards/hkb-push-probe` → `[new reference]`. GitHub accepts
  pushes outside `refs/heads`/`refs/tags`, so the backup property survives the move.
- `git fetch origin '+refs/kb/boards/*:refs/remotes/origin/kb/boards/*'` → landed at
  `refs/remotes/origin/kb/boards/hkb-push-probe`, distinct from the local ref.
- `git show-ref | grep kb-board` and `git ls-remote --heads origin | grep kb-board` → **nothing**. No board
  exists on the old ref yet, here or on the remote, so **there is no migration to write**. This must land
  before this repository's board is migrated (the operator is holding #304 for that), so the board is
  created at the new ref directly.

## What

1. **The ref is `refs/kb/boards/<slug>`**, default `refs/kb/boards/default`. Not `refs/kb/board` with
   `refs/kb/board/<slug>` beside it: git forbids a ref being both a file and a directory prefix, so those
   two could never coexist. `GitTier`'s constructor already takes `ref` as an option — this is mostly the
   default value, plus everything that hardcodes `kb-board`.
2. **The fetch refspec maps into a remote-tracking namespace**:
   `+refs/kb/boards/*:refs/remotes/<remote>/kb/boards/*`. **Not** `refs/kb/*:refs/kb/*` — that would
   overwrite the local board with the remote's copy on every fetch, which is the opposite of what the
   one-writer CAS needs. Measured above.
3. **`tip()`'s read-only fallback** moves from `refs/remotes/<remote>/kb-board` to
   `refs/remotes/<remote>/kb/boards/<slug>`.
4. **`hkb init` writes the refspec** into `.git/config` (`remote.<name>.fetch`, appended, idempotent, never
   replacing the existing `+refs/heads/*` line), and **`hkb doctor` checks it** and names the fix when it is
   missing.
5. **Restore on a fresh clone must still be one command.** A clone has no such refspec — that is the whole
   cost of this option — so `hkb sync` fetches `+refs/kb/boards/*:refs/remotes/<remote>/kb/boards/*`
   explicitly rather than relying on config, and writes the config line while it is there. Restoring a
   board onto a new machine stays: clone, `hkb sync`. That path is tested in
   `test/store-local.test.js` — keep that test passing, it is the durability requirement.
6. **Say the trade in the docs.** `README` ("Backing up and moving a board") and
   `docs/wiki/architecture/kb-board-branch.md` (which needs renaming — the page is about the board's
   durable tier, not about a branch) must say that the board is not visible in GitHub's UI and not fetched
   by a default `git clone`, and why that was chosen.

## Done when

- [ ] No `refs/heads/kb-board` anywhere: `git branch -a` on a board repo shows only the code's branches.
- [ ] A board created, written, pushed, and restored into a fresh clone with `clone` + `hkb sync`.
- [ ] A fetch does not clobber a local board that is ahead of the remote (the refspec mapping, with a test).
- [ ] `hkb doctor` reports a missing refspec and names the fix; `hkb init` writes it idempotently.
- [ ] `hkb sync` works on a clone whose config lacks the refspec.
- [ ] Two boards in one repo (`--board alpha`, `--board beta`) get distinct refs and do not collide.
- [ ] Docs updated, including the page rename.
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test` green.

## Contract

Do not change the tree shape, the write path, or the one-writer rule — this moves *where the ref lives* and
nothing else. Do not write a migration from `refs/heads/kb-board`: measured above, there is nothing on it.
Keep `src/gh.js`/`src/forge.js` the only places that reach the forge. Errors name the fix and carry
`.exitCode`; `--json` everywhere.
title: Move the board off refs/heads: the durable tier lives at refs/kb/boards/<slug>, invisible to git branch
